sentences.cn_text: 在过去二十五年里，英语报纸发生的所有变化中，影响最为深远的也许是其艺术报道在范围和严肃性上不可遏制的衰退。
sentences.en_text: Of all the changes that have taken place in English-language newspapers during the past quarter-century, perhaps the most far-reaching has been the inexorable decline in the scope and seriousness of their arts coverage.

sentences.cn_text: 对于四十岁以下的普通读者而言，要想象大多数大城市报纸曾刊载高质量艺术评论的那个时代，几乎是不可能的。
sentences.en_text: It is difficult to the point of impossibility for the average reader under the age of forty to imagine a time when high-quality arts criticism could be found in most big-city newspapers.

sentences.cn_text: 然而，二十世纪出版的许多最重要的评论集，在很大程度上是由报纸评论构成的。
sentences.en_text: Yet a considerable number of the most significant collections of criticism published in the 20th century consisted in large part of newspaper reviews.

sentences.cn_text: 今天阅读这些著作，不禁会惊叹于其深厚的学术内容曾被认为适宜在面向大众发行的日报上刊载。
sentences.en_text: To read such books today is to marvel at the fact that their learned contents were once deemed suitable for publication in general-circulation dailies.

sentences.cn_text: 我们与二十世纪之交至二战前夕英国发表的那些主题松散的报纸评论相隔更加遥远，彼时新闻纸价格低廉，文雅的艺术评论被视为其所载刊物的装饰。
sentences.en_text: We are even farther removed from the unfocused newspaper reviews published in England between the turn of the 20th century and the eve of World War II, at a time when newsprint was dirt-cheap and stylish arts criticism was considered an ornament to the publications in which it appeared.

sentences.cn_text: 在那些久远的岁月里，主要报纸的评论家详尽而深入地撰写其所报道事件，这被视为理所当然。
sentences.en_text: In those far-off days, it was taken for granted that the critics of major papers would write in detail and at length about the events they covered.

sentences.cn_text: 这是一项严肃的事业,即便是那些不事张扬其学识的评论家,如乔治·伯纳德·萧和欧内斯特·纽曼,也能令人信赖其对本职工作的精通。
sentences.en_text: Theirs was a serious business, and even those reviewers who wore their learning lightly, like George Bernard Shaw and Ernest Newman, could be trusted to know what they were about.

sentences.cn_text: 这些人视新闻业为一种使命，并为能在日报上发表文章而自豪。
sentences.en_text: These men believed in journalism as a calling, and were proud to be published in the daily press.

sentences.cn_text: 纽曼写道:「拥有足够才智或文学天赋以在新闻界立足的作者实在太少，以至于我想将'新闻业'定义为'不为人所读的作家用来蔑称为人所读的作家的一个术语'。」
sentences.en_text: “So few authors have brains enough or literary gift enough to keep their own end up in journalism,” Newman wrote, “that I am tempted to define ‘journalism’ as ‘a term of contempt applied by writers who are not read to writers who are’.”

sentences.cn_text: 遗憾的是，这些评论家几乎已被遗忘。
sentences.en_text: Unfortunately, these critics are virtually forgotten.

sentences.cn_text: 内维尔·卡杜斯自1917年起为《曼彻斯特卫报》撰稿直至1975年去世前不久，如今仅以撰写板球比赛随笔的作者身份为人所知。
sentences.en_text: Neville Cardus, who wrote for the Manchester Guardian from 1917 until shortly before his death in 1975, is now known solely as a writer of essays on the game of cricket.

sentences.cn_text: 然而在其生前，他也是英国最杰出的古典音乐评论家之一，且其文风广受推崇，以至于他的《自传》（1947年）成为畅销之作。
sentences.en_text: During his lifetime, though, he was also one of England’s foremost classical-music critics, and a stylist so widely admired that his Autobiography (1947) became a best-seller.

sentences.cn_text: 1967年他被授予爵士头衔，是首位获此殊荣的音乐评论家。
sentences.en_text: He was knighted in 1967, the first music critic to be so honored.

sentences.cn_text: 然而他的著作中如今仅有一本尚在印行，他那大量音乐论著除专业研究者外无人知晓。
sentences.en_text: Yet only one of his books is now in print, and his vast body of writings on music is unknown save to specialists.

sentences.cn_text: 卡杜斯的评论有可能重获关注吗？
sentences.en_text: Is there any chance that Cardus’s criticism will enjoy a revival?

sentences.cn_text: 这一前景似乎颇为渺茫。
sentences.en_text: The prospect seems remote.

sentences.cn_text: 新闻品味早在他去世前就已改变，而后现代读者对他所擅长的那种雕琢繁复的维多利亚-爱德华风格散文几无用处。
sentences.en_text: Journalistic tastes had changed long before his death, and postmodern readers have little use for the richly upholstered Vicwardian prose in which he specialized.

tokens.gloss: 维多利亚-爱德华时期的

sentences.cn_text: 此外，音乐评论中的业余传统也已急剧式微。
sentences.en_text: Moreover, the amateur tradition in music criticism has been in headlong retreat.

sentences.en_text: It is contemptible for writers to be journalists.

sentences.cn_text: 作家容易受新闻业诱惑。
sentences.en_text: Writers are likely to be tempted into journalism.

sentences.cn_text: 并非所有作家都能胜任新闻写作。
sentences.en_text: Not all writers are capable of journalistic writing.

sentences.cn_text: 根据最后两段，关于卡杜斯可以了解到什么？
sentences.en_text: What can be learned about Cardus according to the last two paragraphs?

sentences.cn_text: 他的音乐评论可能无法吸引今天的读者。
sentences.en_text: His music criticism may not appeal to readers today.

sentences.cn_text: 他作为音乐评论家的声誉长期存在争议。
sentences.en_text: His reputation as a music critic has long been in dispute.

sentences.cn_text: 他的风格主要迎合现代专家。
sentences.en_text: His style caters largely to modern specialists.

sentences.cn_text: 他的作品未能遵循业余传统。
